result:
Both answers come from git runs on the two commits.

- **Ancestor:** No. `git merge-base --is-ancestor side HEAD` printed `NOT-ANCESTOR`. Each branch has its own commit on top of the shared starting point.
- **Conflict:** Yes. `git merge-tree --write-tree HEAD side` exited 1 with `CONFLICT (content): Merge conflict in plans/rebuild/README.md`. Both branches changed line 1 of that file.

I did not merge. `merge-tree` only computes the result and leaves the working tree and index alone.

The two commits are still in place:
- `side` has `f2194adf9`, which sets line 1 to `# claudetto Rebuild Plan (side)`.
- `feat/2.1.327-next` has `ede2d50db`, which sets line 1 to `# claudetto Rebuild Plan (main line)`.

I'm back on `feat/2.1.327-next` and the working tree is clean.

The graph output also shows commits `702f2148a` and `579054ee7` ("Retitle rebuild README on starting branch" and "on side branch"). I didn't make them. They appear to come from other branches that were already in the repo, so I left them alone.
